Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 21

The Volume above a Parabola and below a Slanted Plane

Problem

Use a triple integral to find the volume of the solid enclosed by the parabolic cylinder y=x2 and the planes z=0 and y+z=1.

Reading the solid

The surface y=x2 does not mention z: every vertical line through a point of the parabola y=x2 in the xy-plane belongs to it. So it is a parabolic cylinder that rises from the floor z=0 in the z-direction. The solid is on the concave side of this wall, where y≥x2.

The plane z=0 is the floor. The plane y+z=1 is the roof. Solve the roof equation for z:

y+z=1⟹z=1−y.

The roof is highest over the x-axis, where y=0 gives z=1, and it comes down to the floor at the line y=1. Above the floor the solid exists only where the roof is at or above the floor, that is where 1−y≥0, or y≤1.

The wall and the roof meet where both conditions hold, so the solid projects onto

Dxy​={(x,y):−1≤x≤1,x2≤y≤1},

the region between the parabola y=x2 and the line y=1. The two curves meet at (−1,1) and (1,1), because x2=1 at those two values of x and at no other point.

Above a point of this region the solid runs from the floor z=0 up to the roof z=1−y.

Therefore

E={(x,y,z):−1≤x≤1,x2≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y}.

Two views make the limits visible. The left panel below shows the projection Dxy​, in which x runs from −1 to 1 and y runs from the parabola to the line y=1. The right panel shows the section at x=0.5, which is a triangle in the yz-plane.

Solution

Step 1 — Set up the iterated integral

The volume is the triple integral of 1 over E. The description fixes the order dzdydx: the inner variable is z, the middle variable is y, and the outer variable is x:

V=∭E​1dV=∫−11​∫x21​∫01−y​dzdydx.

Step 2 — Integrate with respect to z

The integrand does not depend on z, so the inner integral is the height of the solid above the point (x,y):

∫01−y​dz=[z]01−y​=1−y.

The height does not depend on x. It equals 1 on the x-axis and falls to 0 at the line y=1.

Step 3 — Integrate with respect to y

Now integrate 1−y from the wall y=x2 up to the ridge y=1:

∫x21​(1−y)dy=[y−2y2​]x21​=(1−21​)−(x2−2x4​)=21​−x2+2x4​.

The result is the area of the triangular section at x, and it depends on x only through x2. At x=0 the section has area 1/2; at x=1 the area is 0, because the triangle has shrunk to a point.

Step 4 — Integrate with respect to x

The outer integral is a polynomial integral:

V=∫−11​(21​−x2+2x4​)dx=[2x​−3x3​+10x5​]−11​.

At x=1 the bracket is

21​−31​+101​=3015​−3010​+303​=308​=154​,

and at x=−1 it is the negative of this value, because every term has an odd power of x. The difference is twice 4/15:

V=154​−(−154​)=158​.

The numerical value is 8/15≈0.533333.

Step 5 — Check with three families of sections

A section at a fixed x is the triangle of Step 3, and its area integrates to 8/15. Two more families give the same value. A section at a fixed height z is the parabolic segment between x=−1−z​ and x=1−z​, with height 1−z−x2. Its area is

A(z)=∫−1−z​1−z​​(1−z−x2)dx=34​(1−z)3/2,

and ∫01​A(z)dz=8/15. A section at a fixed y is a rectangle of width 2y​ and height 1−y, so its area is 2y​(1−y), and ∫01​2y​(1−y)dy=8/15 as well. The three families slice the same solid in three directions, and each sum returns 8/15.

Answer

V=158​≈0.533333.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
∭E​1dVThe triple integral of the constant 1 over E; its value is the volume of E.
EThe solid of integration: the points with −1≤x≤1, x2≤y≤1, and 0≤z≤1−y.
dV=dzdydxThe volume element in Cartesian coordinates, the product of the three coordinate differentials in the chosen order.
parabolic cylinder y=x2The surface made by moving the parabola y=x2 parallel to the z-axis; it is the wall of the solid.
z=0The floor of the solid, the xy-plane.
y+z=1The roof of the solid; solved for z it gives the height z=1−y.
Dxy​The projection of E onto the xy-plane, the region between the parabola y=x2 and the line y=1.
1−yThe height of the solid above the point (x,y); it does not depend on x.
A(z)The area of the section at a fixed height z, a parabolic segment of area 34​(1−z)3/2.
ΔxThe thickness of one slice in the figure; the slices approximate E, and the sum of their volumes becomes the integral as Δx→0.

Verification

Three independent computations support the result.

  • part1_step1.py checks the three bounding surfaces and estimates the volume by Monte Carlo sampling in the box −1≤x≤1, 0≤y≤1, 0≤z≤1, whose volume is 2.0. The estimate is 0.53293 against 0.53333, a deviation of −0.92 standard errors with standard error 0.00044. The sampled points fall inside the solid with fraction 0.26646, close to the ratio (8/15)/2. The script also reports the wall values x2 at five values of x and the roof heights 1.0000, 0.5000, and 0.0000 at y=0, y=0.5, and y=1.
  • part1_step2.py evaluates the integral with SymPy. It returns the inner integral x4/2−x2+1/2, the antiderivative x5/10−x3/3+x/2, the values 4/15 and −4/15 at x=1 and x=−1, and the volume 8/15=0.533333. The section checks return the areas x4/2−x2+1/2, 4(1−z)3/2/3, and 2y​(1−y), and each of the three integrates to 8/15. At x=0.5 the section area is 0.28125, with edges y=0.25000 and z=0.75000.
  • part1_step3.py evaluates the volume with mpmath quadrature at 25 digits in two orders, projection first and sections first. Both values are 0.533333333333333, with a deviation of 0.0 from 8/15.
